languages.approach: The first lesson is not a lesson. It is a conversation. I want to know what you do, what you are interested in, and how you actually learn, because a person who learns by talking needs a different hour from a person who learns by writing things down. After that I build the course around you. Your work, your hobbies, the situations you will really be in.
languages.specialTitle: Two things I am asked for most

special.d: For pilots and aspiring pilots, wherever you are. We work on the language of radio communication, on the physics and the mechanics of flight, and on the vocabulary you need to be precise under pressure. Grammar where grammar is the thing getting in the way. Then role plays, exercises and tasks, because in a cockpit you do not get to prepare your sentence first.

British and American English for the situations your job actually puts you in. Speaking up in a weekly check-in without rehearsing it in your head first. Presenting to a room and keeping it. Holding a conversation at a conference when the small talk matters as much as the agenda. We work on the register, the filler phrases that buy you a second, and the difference between sounding fluent and sounding sure of yourself.

languages.sampleText: Take a look at how a class actually runs before you book anything. Each sample is a real lesson plan, not a brochure.

faq.q: What does a brand strategist actually do?
faq.a: A brand strategist decides what a business should stand for, who it speaks to and how it says it, before any design or advertising begins. In practice that means positioning, a messaging structure, and a tone of voice. Design makes a brand look consistent. Strategy makes it mean something consistent.

faq.q: What is the difference between translation and cultural adaptation?
faq.a: Translation carries words across languages. Adaptation carries meaning across markets. The same claim does different work in different places: quality reads as engineering and reliability in German, and closer to care and craftsmanship in Italian. A translated tagline can be correct and still land flat. Adaptation rewrites for the effect the original was designed to have, which usually means changing the words.

A website and visibility check is €150. Local visibility setup is €450. Brand strategy and ongoing support are quoted on request, because the scope varies far more than a website does. Websites start at €900.

faq.q: Do you work with clients outside Italy?
faq.a: Yes. I work remotely by default and travel across Europe for on-site work and events.

faq.q: What does SEO have to do with brand strategy?
faq.a: Search is where positioning gets tested. Keyword research shows the words your market actually uses for its problem, and those are often not the words a business uses for its solution. Closing that gap improves rankings and sharpens the brand at the same time.

about.title: About Victoria Clara Swart
about.description: Web designer, brand strategist and language teacher in Rome. Market and Management Anthropology, five languages, websites written and coded by one person.
about.lead: I grew up in East Frisia, in the north of Germany, between a Frisian family on my father's side and a Volga German family on my mother's, so more than one language was always in the room. At sixteen I spent a year in Colombia and taught my first English class there. Since then I have lived and worked in Denmark, Spain and Italy, studied Market and Management Anthropology, and learned to build websites in code.
about.shaped: Anthropology taught me to watch how people actually behave before deciding what to say to them. Code lets me build the thing myself instead of describing it to someone else. Languages let me do both for people in five countries at once. I build bridges between languages, cultures, business and technology.
about.stage: You'll also find me on stage, hosting and moderating international conferences and pitch events.

This site sets no cookies. It uses no analytics and no tracking of any kind.

When you send the form, your name, email address and message are processed by Formspree and forwarded to me by email. The form also records which language version of the site you used, and, if you arrived from a link on a client's website, which site sent you. That data is used only to answer you. It is not sold and not shared for marketing.

If you are offered a different language version, that suggestion comes from your browser's own language setting. No location lookup is done on your IP address and nothing is sent to a third party. Your choice is stored in your browser's local storage, which is not a cookie and never leaves your device.
Fonts are served from this site's own server. No request is made to Google Fonts or any other font service.
If you are in the EU or EEA you can ask to see, correct or delete any personal data you have sent me. Write to victoria.c.swart@icloud.com and I will answer within the period the law allows.
Form messages are kept only as long as needed to answer you and to keep a record of the work that followed.
